Actions of our employees, directors, third-party contractors or suppliers could expose us to reputational risks.
Growth in large load customers, including data centers, may increase customer concentration, capital requirements and revenue variability risks.
Our ability to reliably serve customer demand depends on the availability of sufficient generation and capacity resources.

We could suffer negative impacts to our reputation as a result of actual or perceived fraud, misconduct, legal or regulatory violations, violations of corporate policies, inappropriate use of social media, or other actions by our employees, directors …
Regulators may challenge rate increases due to increased customer affordability pressures.
Additional demand from a limited number of customers may increase our credit risk exposure and require incremental infrastructure investment.
Advancements in artificial intelligence and large language models may increase cybersecurity threats and operational risks.

removed.t: Our employees, directors, third-party contractors, or suppliers may violate or be perceived to violate our Codes of Conduct, which could have an adverse effect on our reputation.
Adverse regulatory rulings (including changes in recovery mechanisms) or the imposition of additional regulations could negatively impact our results of operations, financial condition or cash flows.
The Board of Directors is responsible for the oversight of material risk and maintaining an effective risk monitoring process.
Xcel Energy maintains a robust compliance program and promotes a culture of compliance beginning with the tone at the top.
Management identifies and analyzes risks to determine materiality and other attributes such as timing, probability and controllability.

Management also identifies and analyzes risk through the business planning process, development of goals and establishment of key performance indicators, including identification of barriers to implementing Xcel Energy's strategy.
Management communicates regularly with the Board of Directors and key stakeholders regarding risk.
The oversight, management and mitigation of risk is an integral and continuous part of the Board of Directors' governance of Xcel Energy.
The Audit Committee is responsible for reviewing the adequacy of the committees' risk oversight and affirming appropriate aggregate oversight occurs.
Emerging risks are considered and assigned as appropriate during the annual Board of Directors and committee evaluation process, resulting in updates to the committee charters and annual work plans.

We have programs in place to mitigate the physical and financial risks associated with wildfires; however, Xcel Energy's wildfire mitigation initiatives may not be successful or effective in preventing or reducing wildfire-related losses.
In addition, Xcel Energy cannot fully assure that its controls will be effective against all potential risks.
We are exposed to risk of employee or third-party contractor fraud or misconduct.
Xcel Energy does not tolerate discrimination, violations of our Code of Conduct or other unacceptable behaviors.
Generative Artificial Intelligence, such as large language models like ChatGPT, present a range of challenges and potential risks as we consider impacts to the business.
